anomalies.observed: On the top connector J2 the +5V net is attached to pin 27 (with pin 25 labelled PIN25 / unconnected), but on the bottom connector J1 the +5V label sits on the pin-25 row and the pin-27 row is left unconnected. The two 2x15 bus connectors therefore do not carry identical pin-to-net assignments on the 5V line.
anomalies.expected: The specification states J1 and J2 have 'identical nets on both so the board can be stacked ... (pass-through)' and that 'The same +5V net is also tied directly to J1/J2 pin 27'. Both connectors must present +5V on pin 27 and leave pin 25 as the same (unconnected) PIN25 net.

evidence.quote: identical nets on both so the board can be stacked between the M5Stack Core and a lower module (pass-through). Carries +5V, +3V3, BAT, GND, GPIO/UART pins
The same +5V net is also tied directly to J1/J2 pin 27 (the M5Stack bus's 5V pin)
Sheet m5-pantilt: J2 left column bottom rows read PIN25(25), +5V(27), BAT(29); J1 left column bottom rows read +5V(25), [blank](27), BAT(29)

anomalies.impact: When the board is stacked on an M5Stack Core, the Core's pin 25 signal line is shorted to the board's +5V rail, while the Core's 5V (pin 27) is left open on J1, so the 5V rail no longer passes through to J1 and the Core's 5V does not feed the board via that connector. This can damage the Core's GPIO/DAC pin and break the 5V pass-through and external-supply OR-ing.

parsed.summary: Most of the schematic matches the specification (values, jumper network, MAX3485/UART path, D1/D2 diode directions, bulk caps, battery switch), but the +5V net is pinned to J1 pin 25 instead of pin 27, breaking the 'identical nets on both connectors' pass-through requirement and shorting the 5V rail onto a bus signal pin.
